title: How to Visit Northland on a Family Budget – 3-Day Guide
meta_desc: Discover how to explore Northland’s Cape Reinga, Ninety Mile Beach and kauri forests on a family budget of $200‑$380 a day, with free activities, affordable stays and smart splurges.
intro: Northland packs iconic landmarks, ancient forests and endless beaches into a compact region that’s easy to explore with kids. With a little planning you can enjoy the highlights without blowing the family budget.

sections.heading: Budget at a Glance
sections.body:
For a family of four, aim for $200‑$380 per day. The biggest line items are accommodation ($80‑$150), meals ($70‑$120) and transport ($30‑$60). The remaining cash can cover activity fees, fuel and occasional treats.

Keeping a simple spreadsheet helps you stay on track, especially when you’re moving between coastal towns where prices vary.
list: Buffer for souvenirs or unexpected costs: $20‑$30/day

sections.heading: Where to Stay: Cheap to Mid‑Range
sections.body:
Northland offers a range of family‑friendly lodgings. Holiday parks with powered sites are the cheapest option, while boutique motels give a touch of comfort without breaking the bank.

Book early in shoulder season (April‑May, September‑October) to snag the best rates and avoid the summer rush.
list: Holiday park cabins (e.g., Whangarei Top 10 Holiday Park): $80‑$100/night, kitchen facilities, kids’ playground.
Budget motels (e.g., Bayview Motel, Kaitaia): $110‑$130/night, free Wi‑Fi, close to main attractions.
Mid‑range lodges (e.g., The Lodge at Opononi): $150‑$180/night, en‑suite rooms, on‑site BBQs, stunning beach views.

sections.heading: Free & Low‑Cost Activities
sections.body:
Northland’s natural wonders are largely free. Pack a picnic and let the kids roam the sand, forests and historic sites without spending a cent.

When you do need equipment, the costs are modest and worth the experience.
list: Cape Reinga walkway – 30‑minute return to the tip (free).
Ninety Mile Beach – walk, watch the surf, or enjoy a sunrise (free; 4WD hire optional $120‑$150/day).
Mangawhai Heads beach walk and estuary (free).
Kauri Museum (Matakohe) – kids under 5 free, adults $12, family pass $35.
Sandboarding at Ninety Mile Beach – board hire $15‑$20 per person.
Hokianga Harbour dunes – free to explore, bring your own kite or frisbee.

sections.heading: Splurge Worth It
sections.body:
Some experiences add depth to your trip and are worth the extra spend. They’re usually limited in availability, so pre‑book where possible.

These splurges create lasting memories without inflating the overall daily budget dramatically.
list: Guided Maori cultural tour at Waitangi Treaty Grounds – $45 per adult, $25 per child (includes performance and museum entry).
4WD hire for a day to drive the full length of Ninety Mile Beach – $130‑$150, includes insurance.
Kayak tour of Mangawhai Harbour – $60 per person for a 2‑hour guided trip.
Stay in a beachfront cabin at Tokerau Bay – $180‑$210/night for a night of ‘off‑the‑grid’ luxury.
